key_insight: Twisted, coherently bonded lithium niobate interfaces form nanoscale structural helices separated by screw dislocations, with torsional strain implying chiral dipolar helices rather than simple moiré patterns.
engineering_relevance: Coupled elastic deformation, dislocations and ferroelectric polarization offer a route to chiral oxide interfaces and a distinct form of twistronics.
method: Map interfacial contrast using 4D STEM and differential phase contrast imaging.
Model electron channeling along helical pathways and directly image structural helices using electron ptychography.
Assess chirality through sample-inversion imaging and second-harmonic optical circular dichroism.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports directly imaged structural helices, unchanged DPC images after sample inversion and unusually large interfacial optical dichroism signals.
watch_item: Dipolar helices are inferred from electromechanical coupling rather than directly imaged, and device-level performance is not established in the abstract.
